denial_codes.label: MTB Reached
denial_codes.description: Maximum Therapy Benefit reached — payer claims patient has plateaued and further therapy is not medically necessary.

appeal_strategy.primary_argument: Patient has NOT reached maximum benefit — documented objective improvements in standardized outcome measures demonstrate continued skilled need.
key_evidence: Standardized outcome measures showing continued improvement (FOTO, DASH, LEFS, NDI, ODI)
Objective data trending toward established functional goals
Exercise progression documentation (resistance, reps, complexity increases)
Functional milestone documentation (e.g., return to ADLs, work tasks)
Clinical reasoning for continued skilled intervention
cms_citations: CMS Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 15, §220.2 — Reasonable and necessary skilled services
CMS Chapter 15, §220.2(B) — Expectation of improvement is NOT required; maintenance therapy qualifies if skilled care is needed
CMS Chapter 15, §220.3 — Coverage does not turn on the presence or absence of a patient's potential for improvement
oon_arguments: Out-of-network provider selected by patient for specialized expertise
Assignment of Benefits (AOB) on file — provider authorized to bill and appeal on patient's behalf
Medical necessity determination must be based on clinical evidence, not network status

required_documentation: Initial evaluation with baseline outcome measures
Progress notes showing objective improvement trends
Standardized outcome measure scores (at least 2 data points)
Updated plan of care with measurable goals
Exercise progression log

denial_codes.label: Non-Skilled
denial_codes.description: Services deemed non-skilled — payer claims treatment could be performed by patient or non-licensed caregiver.

appeal_strategy.primary_argument: Services require the clinical judgment and expertise of a licensed therapist — cannot be safely or effectively self-administered.
key_evidence: Clinical reasoning documentation for each intervention
Real-time modification documentation (adjusted technique, resistance, positioning during session)
Safety concerns requiring skilled supervision (fall risk, pain responses, compensatory patterns)
Complexity of condition requiring ongoing clinical assessment
Patient education components requiring professional instruction
cms_citations: CMS Chapter 15, §220.2(B) — Services are skilled when they require the expertise of a qualified therapist
CMS Chapter 15, §220.2(D) — Skilled therapy services include ongoing assessment and modification
Jimmo v. Sebelius Settlement (2013) — Maintenance therapy requiring skilled care is covered
oon_arguments: Out-of-network provider selected for specialized manual therapy techniques
AOB on file authorizing provider to bill and appeal
Skilled nature of services is determined by clinical complexity, not provider network status

required_documentation: Detailed visit notes with clinical reasoning for each intervention
Documentation of real-time modifications during treatment
Safety assessment and fall risk documentation
Rationale for why services cannot be self-administered
Patient response to treatment requiring clinical interpretation

denial_codes.label: Re-eval Bundled
denial_codes.description: Re-evaluation bundled into treatment — payer denies separate payment for re-evaluation CPT code, claiming it is included in treatment visit.

appeal_strategy.primary_argument: Re-evaluation was medically necessary due to a triggering event and constitutes a comprehensive reassessment distinct from routine treatment.
key_evidence: Triggering event documentation (change in condition, new diagnosis, post-surgical, return from absence)
Comprehensive reassessment evidence (new objective measurements, updated baselines)
Distinct ICD-10 codes or new clinical findings
New or substantially revised plan of care resulting from re-evaluation
CPT code distinction: 97164/97168 vs treatment codes
cms_citations: CPT Guidelines — Re-evaluation (97164/97168) is distinct from treatment and requires a triggering event
CMS Chapter 15, §220.1 — Re-evaluation is a covered service when clinically indicated
NCCI Edits — 97164/97168 are not inherently bundled with treatment codes when documented appropriately
oon_arguments: Re-evaluation necessity is a clinical determination independent of network status
AOB on file — provider authorized to bill separately for distinct services
Bundling edit applied incorrectly — triggering event and comprehensive reassessment documented

required_documentation: Documentation of triggering event with date
Comprehensive re-evaluation with new objective measurements
Comparison of previous vs. current status
New or revised plan of care with updated goals
Distinct time documentation for re-eval vs. treatment on same day

denial_codes.label: Dup Eval
denial_codes.description: Duplicate evaluation — payer denies evaluation claiming a prior evaluation already exists for this patient/condition.

appeal_strategy.primary_argument: This evaluation is for a new episode of care, distinct diagnosis, or different body region — not a duplicate of the prior evaluation.
key_evidence: New episode of care documentation (prior episode discharged/closed)
Distinct ICD-10 diagnosis codes from prior evaluation
Different body region or clinical presentation
New referral or prescription from physician
Provider change justification (if applicable)
cms_citations: CPT Guidelines — New evaluation is appropriate for new episode of care or new condition
CMS Chapter 15, §220.1 — Initial evaluation is covered for each new episode of care
NCCI Edits — Evaluation codes are not duplicative when clinical distinction is documented
oon_arguments: Episode of care determination is clinical, not administrative
AOB on file — provider authorized to evaluate and bill for distinct episodes
Prior evaluation by different provider/setting does not preclude new evaluation for new episode

required_documentation: Prior episode discharge summary or documentation of closure
New referral or physician prescription
Distinct ICD-10 codes or new clinical presentation
Documentation of different body region or condition (if applicable)
New evaluation with independent baseline measurements
